title: AdeptAds Releases Agent Skills for Google Ads Automation
summary: AdeptAds launches open-source agent skills and Claude/Codex plugins enabling AI agents to manage Google Ads campaigns autonomously via API integration.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- AdeptAds released open-source agent skills that let Claude and Codex agents create, optimize, and manage Google Ads campaigns programmatically.
- The toolkit provides API integration primitives for campaign creation, bid management, keyword research, and performance analysis through structured agent actions.
- Developers can now build autonomous advertising agents that handle end-to-end campaign workflows without manual Google Ads Console interaction.


AdeptAds has released an open-source toolkit that enables AI agents to manage Google Ads campaigns autonomously. The agent skills package, now available on GitHub, provides structured primitives for Claude and Codex agents to interact with the Google Ads API, handling everything from campaign creation to performance optimization without requiring developers to write custom integration code.


The release addresses a persistent friction point in AI-driven marketing automation: translating natural language agent intent into concrete Google Ads API calls. Rather than forcing developers to build bespoke connectors, AdeptAds ships pre-built skills that agents can invoke through standardized function calls.


## What the toolkit includes


The agent skills package provides four core capability clusters. Campaign management skills let agents create new campaigns, adjust budgets, pause underperforming ad groups, and modify targeting parameters. Keyword research skills enable agents to discover relevant search terms, analyze competition levels, and generate negative keyword lists based on conversion data.


Bid optimization skills allow agents to adjust cost-per-click targets dynamically based on performance thresholds, while analytics skills provide structured access to impression data, click-through rates, conversion metrics, and quality scores. Each skill exposes a clean JSON schema that Claude and Codex agents can call directly, with built-in error handling and rate limiting to respect Google Ads API quotas.


- Campaign creation and budget allocation via structured JSON parameters
- Automated bid adjustments based on real-time performance signals
- Keyword discovery and negative keyword management workflows
- Performance reporting with customizable date ranges and metric filters


## Technical implementation details


The toolkit uses OAuth 2.0 for Google Ads authentication and maintains session state across agent interactions. Developers authenticate once with their Google Ads account credentials, and the skills package handles token refresh automatically. The repository includes example agent prompts that demonstrate how to chain multiple skills into coherent workflows, such as launching a new product campaign with automated A/B testing of ad copy variations.


AdeptAds designed the skills to work with both Claude and Codex agent frameworks, exposing the same function signatures regardless of the underlying model. This cross-platform compatibility means developers can switch between Claude's reasoning capabilities and Codex's code generation strengths without rewriting integration logic.


## Release date and availability


Officially released on November 11, 2026, the agent skills package is distributed under an MIT license. The GitHub repository includes comprehensive documentation, sample workflows, and a Docker container for local testing against the Google Ads sandbox environment. AdeptAds plans to maintain the toolkit as the Google Ads API evolves, with community contributions welcomed via pull requests.


## What this means for advertising automation


This release lowers the barrier for developers building autonomous marketing agents. Previously, integrating AI agents with advertising platforms required weeks of API documentation study and custom connector development. AdeptAds' skills package compresses that timeline to hours, enabling smaller teams to experiment with agent-driven campaign strategies. As Claude and Codex agents become more sophisticated at multi-step reasoning, toolkits like this will determine which business workflows become fully autonomous versus semi-automated. The open-source model also invites rapid iteration, with the advertising community able to contribute skills for emerging Google Ads features like Performance Max campaigns or demand forecasting endpoints.
